description: PREP-SHOT is a Python energy-expansion model developed by the PREP-NexT laboratory at the National University of Singapore. Linear programming couples multi-zone capacity and transmission planning with short-term hydropower operation to meet demand at minimum cost. Inputs use Excel with JSON scenario configuration, and outputs use NetCDF through xarray. Operational time steps can be hourly. The reusable model has global applicability; its documented Lower Mekong example covers five countries and 57 cascading hydropower stations under a 2030 carbon constraint. Public source and run instructions are free under GPL-3.0. HiGHS is the default open solver, with optional commercial solver interfaces carrying separate terms. A limitation is that expanding conventional hydropower, converting plants to pumped storage and retrofitting carbon capture are still listed as planned. The authors also caution against precise operational prediction. PREP-SHOT supports coupled water-energy planning and can be compared with energy-expansion models such as PyPSA (model-pypsa). Its Nature Water article describes the balancing-oriented hydropower application. No basin dataset or optimisation run was obtained.
